pages.title: About
pages.content:
ABOUT THE SCHOOL

About

Hibari Flight School has trained from Hangar 2 at Brackmoor Airfield since 2011. Margit Halvorsen and Ruth Abernathy opened it with two aircraft and a habit they still teach: read the wind, then fly.

Hangar 2, 2011

Hibari Flight School opened in 2011 in Hangar 2 at Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale. Margit Halvorsen, head of training, and Ruth Abernathy, chief engineer, founded it with two aircraft. The field they started on is the field students still use: runway 09/27, grass 780 m and asphalt 640 m. Flying runs Tuesday to Sunday, from 08:00 to sunset. The office is open Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00, and the field is closed on Monday.

The phone is +1 555 0142 0911 and the desk writes from hello@hibariflight.example. The school is still in that hangar. Lessons still begin with the wind on the boundary and a person beside the student, on the grass of a regional airfield, before anyone talks about a licence form.

Why a lark

The school is named for the lark. Hibari is the lark, and the bird is the mark on the hangar door and the small drawing perched at the edge of photographs. A lark commits to the air only after it has read it. That is the whole method, and it is the line on the first screen: read the wind, then fly. The orange windsock on the boundary is the instrument that sentence points to.

Students look at it on the way in, and the instructor points to it again before a trial flight or a lesson. Training here is meant to feel like a morning with a person beside you, not like a technical brochure. The drawn lark simply stays on the edge of that morning and reminds you which way the wind is going.

How a lesson is taught

Every lesson flies the same shape: brief, walk round, fly, debrief. One block is two hours on the field. Twenty-five minutes are the brief, twenty minutes the walk-round, sixty minutes the flight and fifteen minutes the debrief. Seventy minutes of that block are in the air or on the way to it. The circuit itself is the rounded pattern students see drawn in the clubhouse and then fly from runway 09/27.

Margit Halvorsen has kept this outline since 2011. Instructors who joined later teach the same outline. The wind changes. The order of the morning does not. Repetition is how the checks, the lookout and the judgement of a landing become familiar, on grass 780 m and asphalt 640 m, with the windsock in sight.

2011, 2015, 2019, 2024

2011

Margit Halvorsen and Ruth Abernathy opened Hangar 2 with two aircraft.

2015

the school was still teaching that circuit from the same hangar. Tomás Ferreira had joined as a flight instructor in 2014, so by 2015 he was already part of the flying week.

2019

Ines Laurent arrived to run operations and bookings, which is still her work, on +1 555 0142 0911.

2024

the seven people on the crew page were already in their jobs. The last of them, Jonah Petrakis, had come in 2021 to teach tailwheel and cross-country.

These dates record who was here. They are not a list of prizes, and they are not a timetable for how quickly a student will finish.

Walk the field with us on a trial flight morning.

Contact the office →

pages.title: Licences
pages.content:
PPL, LAPL AND NIGHT RATING

Licences

Hibari Flight School teaches the PPL, the LAPL and a night rating taken after the PPL. The hours below are minima and usual ranges, not a date the school can stamp in advance.

Private Pilot Licence

The Private Pilot Licence, the PPL, has a minimum of 45 hours. At Hibari Flight School it usually takes 9 to 14 months. Most students fly 50 to 60 hours before the test. Budget from $13,500. That budget is an estimate, not a promise, because weather and how often you come both change the total. Dual time on the two-seat trainers is $245 per flight hour, with aircraft, fuel and instructor.

Solo hire is $195 per flight hour. A prepaid bundle of 10 flight hours is $2,350. Ground school, the PPL theory course, is 10 evenings at $680. Winter ground school begins on 2026.12.02, Tuesday and Thursday, 19:00 to 21:00, and Aisha Rahman leads it. Licence test aircraft hire, up to 2 hours, is $440. The examiner's fee is paid to the examiner.

LAPL

The LAPL minimum is 30 hours, and students here usually take 6 to 10 months. Budget from $9,200. That figure is an estimate, not a fixed quote. The aircraft are the same two-seat low-wing trainers, the airfield is still Brackmoor, and the circuit is still the one flown from runway 09/27. Dual lessons remain $245 per flight hour and solo hire remains $195. The prepaid 10-hour block remains $2,350 if you would rather pay that way.

The lesson shape does not shrink for the LAPL: brief, walk-round, fly and debrief stay in that order. Some students choose the LAPL because the minimum hours and the usual span of months are shorter. If you are not sure which licence you want, book the trial flight first and decide after you have sat in the aircraft.

Night rating

The night rating is 5 flight hours, taken after the PPL. The course is $1,350. Kwame Mensah leads it and has been an instructor at the school since 2018. Five hours is the length of the course as the school sells it. It is not a promise about how many weeks the calendar will need if the weather keeps a morning on the ground. Book the course through the office, Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00, on +1 555 0142 0911 or hello@hibariflight.example.

A night-rating flight is still briefed and still debriefed. The windsock, the direction of runway 09/27 and the state of the sky belong in that brief, as they do on a daylight lesson. Field flying hours remain Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset. The office will place the five hours inside the published rules of the field.

PATH

Four steps in this order. Nobody is handed a finish date.

01

Trial flight

40 min

Forty minutes airborne with a briefing, $190. A first look at the controls and the field.

02

Ground school & dual

10 evenings

PPL theory is ten evenings at $680. Dual lessons run alongside at $245 per flight hour.

03

First solo

15–20 h

Usually after 15 to 20 hours, when your instructor decides the circuit is yours to fly alone.

04

Cross-country & test

up to 2 h

Navigation in the four-seat tourer, then the licence test with aircraft hire of up to 2 hours at $440.

Fees in full →

From trial flight to the test

The path has four steps, and the school keeps them in this order. Trial flight first. Then ground school and dual together. Then first solo, usually after 15 to 20 hours. Then cross-country and the licence test. Priya Nair, written up in Stories, flew her first solo at 18 hours, inside that usual band. Cross-country uses the four-seat touring aircraft as well as the trainers.

Elena Duarte's story is a flight from Brackmoor to Calder Field, 74 nm. The test itself uses aircraft hire of up to 2 hours at $440, and the examiner's fee is paid separately to the examiner. No step arrives with a finish date attached. The usual span is 9 to 14 months for the PPL and 6 to 10 months for the LAPL, and usual is the honest word.

Do I need a medical before I start?

For a licence, yes, and you arrange it yourself. The PPL path uses a Class 2 medical. The LAPL uses a LAPL medical. Both come from an aviation medical examiner, and the student books the appointment. Hibari Flight School does not book it and does not charge for it. A trial flight is a different gate. Visitors can fly with an instructor from the age of 14, up to 110 kg, without that medical.

If you only want to read the wind for forty minutes, start with the trial at $190 and leave the medical until you know you want to continue. Questions about which medical fits which licence can go to the office on +1 555 0142 0911 or hello@hibariflight.example during office hours, Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00.

Start with forty minutes airborne.

pages.title: Lesson block
pages.content:
HOW A LESSON IS FLOWN

Lesson block

A lesson block at Hibari Flight School is two hours on the field at Brackmoor. The four parts always run in the same order, and they always take the same times.

Two hours on the field

One block is two hours on the field. Seventy minutes of it are in the air or on the way to it. The four parts are brief 25 min, walk-round 20 min, fly 60 min and debrief 15 min. Together they are the two hours. You meet your instructor at Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, on a flying day, Tuesday to Sunday, from 08:00 to sunset. The pattern you fly is the same circuit every lesson uses, off runway 09/27.

Dual flying is $245 per flight hour and includes aircraft, fuel, instructor and landing fees at Brackmoor. A prepaid lesson block bundle is 10 flight hours for $2,350. The bundle is how those hours are paid for. It is not a different shape of morning. Each time you come, the block still runs in the same four parts.

LESSON

Brief, walk-round, fly, debrief. Two hours on the field, every time.

01

Brief

25 min

Weather, the circuit and the goal for the flight, talked through with your instructor.

02

Walk-round

20 min

Hands along the wing, a fuel sample to the light, every hinge checked together.

03

Fly

60 min

Climb out from runway 09/27 and fly the circuit, or the exercise you briefed.

04

Debrief

15 min

Headsets off beside the parked aircraft. What matched the brief, said plainly.

Brief, 25 minutes

The brief is 25 minutes, and it happens before anyone walks to the aircraft. Instructor and student sit down and agree what this flight is for. The instructor sketches the circuit, the rounded pattern with the wind on one leg, and the two of them talk through the checks and the runway. The student is expected to have looked at the windsock and the sky already. The clubhouse window faces the apron, and a cup of coffee is a normal part of the table. Twenty-five minutes is enough to name the lesson and to make the weather call. It is not ground school. The PPL theory course is a separate booking of 10 evenings at $680. The brief is about the aeroplane you are about to fly, in the wind that is on the boundary this morning.

Walk-round, 20 minutes

The walk-round is 20 minutes. Instructor and student check the aircraft together. Hands go along the wing, onto the aileron hinge, and around the rest of the airframe. A fuel sample is held up to the light. The student is learning the sequence by doing it, with the instructor beside them. This time still belongs to the two-hour block, on the grass or the apron at Brackmoor, before the 60 minutes in the air. The aircraft is one of the three two-seat low-wing trainers, or the four-seat touring aircraft when the lesson is cross-country. Wear shoes you can walk in and clothes you can climb the wing walk in. Come in time for the brief so these twenty minutes are calm. Ruth Abernathy's engineering is what the walk-round is trusting, every flying day.

Fly, 60 minutes

The flight is 60 minutes. It is the airborne part of the block, inside the seventy minutes that are in the air or on the way to it. Most lessons stay in the circuit from runway 09/27, grass 780 m and asphalt 640 m. A navigation lesson leaves the circuit. Jonah Petrakis teaches tailwheel and cross-country, and cross-country uses the four-seat touring aircraft. Ordinary dual lessons use the two-seat trainers. Once you are sent solo, solo hire is $195 per flight hour. A first solo usually comes after 15 to 20 hours. Priya Nair's was at 18 hours. None of that is decided inside a single brief. For this hour the work is the lesson you planned: the wind on the windsock, the checks you agreed, and the landing you will talk about when the engine is quiet.

Debrief, 15 minutes

The debrief is 15 minutes. After the aircraft is shut down, instructor and student stay beside it. Headsets come off. They talk through what matched the brief and what did not. Fifteen minutes is short on purpose, while the detail is still easy to remember. The next morning can be named before anyone leaves the apron. Ines Laurent runs operations and bookings if you want the office to hold that date. The office is open Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00, on +1 555 0142 0911 and at hello@hibariflight.example. The debrief is not a theory paper and it is not the 10-evening ground school. It is the last part of the same block, and it closes the shape the school has flown since 2011: brief, walk-round, fly, debrief.

What if the weather is below minima?

If the morning is below the school's minima, Hibari Flight School cancels by 07:00 and there is no charge. The flight is rebooked free. A prepaid hour in the 10-hour block is not used. The same rule covers a trial flight: weather cancellations by 07:00, rebooked free. The desk will tell you it is below minima. You do not have to decide that from a forecast on your own.

Flying days stay Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset, and Monday the field is closed. When the day is on, wear plain clothes you can sit in for an hour, closed shoes for the grass, and a warm layer from autumn onward. Bring photo identification when the booking asks for it. A trial flight always asks: arrive 30 minutes early, with photo ID, from age 14, up to 110 kg.

Fly your first block with a trial flight.

pages.title: Trial flight
pages.content:
40 MINUTES AIRBORNE

Trial flight

A trial flight is 40 minutes airborne with a briefing, in a two-seat trainer from Brackmoor Airfield. The price is $190, and it is the usual way to start.

Forty minutes airborne

The trial flight is 40 minutes in the air, with a briefing, and it costs $190. The price is in USD and includes aircraft, fuel, instructor and landing fees at Brackmoor. You fly from Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale, in a two-seat low-wing trainer. The morning follows the school's shape in a shorter form: look at the wind, brief, walk to the aircraft, fly, and talk afterwards. It does not start the 45-hour PPL minimum and it is not a shortened licence course.

It is a visit in which you sit in the cockpit, fasten a headset, and feel the circuit with an instructor beside you. The instructor will point out the windsock. The next trial-flight morning on the field board is 2026.11.15, from 08:30 to 12:00. Martin Okonjo's story, A first trial flight on a still Saturday, is one visitor's account of this flight.

Who can take a trial flight?

A trial flight is open from the age of 14, up to a weight of 110 kg. Those are the limits for this booking. You do not need a Class 2 medical or a LAPL medical to fly the trial. Those medicals belong to students who go on to a licence, and you book them yourself with an aviation medical examiner when you reach that point. You do need to arrive 30 minutes early with photo identification.

Wear shoes you can walk the apron in, and clothes you can sit in under a headset. If you already hope to train for the PPL or the LAPL, the trial is still the right first step. The path after it is ground school and dual, then first solo, usually after 15 to 20 hours, then cross-country and the licence test. The morning itself does not commit you to any of that.

BOOKING

Four steps from choosing a morning to flying it. Weather cancellations by 07:00 are rebooked free.

01

Choose a morning

online or phone

Pick a Tuesday to Sunday morning online, or call +1 555 0142 0911 and ask for Ines.

02

Confirmation

1 working day

A confirmation e-mail reaches you within one working day with the time and where to park.

03

On the day

30 min early

Arrive 30 minutes early with photo ID. Walk round the aircraft with your instructor.

04

Fly

40 min

Forty minutes airborne with a briefing, and your hands on the controls over Alder Vale.

Contact the office →

How does booking work?

There are four steps. First, choose a morning online or by phone on +1 555 0142 0911. Second, a confirmation e-mail arrives within one working day, from hello@hibariflight.example. Third, on the day, arrive 30 minutes early with photo identification. Fourth, fly. The office takes calls Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00. The field is open for flying Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset, and it is closed on Monday.

If the weather is below minima, the school cancels by 07:00, there is no charge, and the morning is rebooked free. Ines Laurent looks after operations and bookings. The trial-flight morning written on the field board is 2026.11.15, 08:30 to 12:00, at the usual price of $190. Choosing that morning, or another one, is the whole of step one.

Can I give a trial flight as a gift?

Yes. A trial flight can be given as a gift at the same price, $190, for 40 minutes airborne with a briefing. Call +1 555 0142 0911 or write to hello@hibariflight.example and say that it is a gift. The bookings desk will confirm a morning within one working day, just as it does for any other trial, and the confirmation can go to the person you name. The visitor still arrives 30 minutes early with photo identification.

The same limits apply: age 14 or over, and up to 110 kg. The recipient does not have to choose a licence on the day. If they later want the PPL theory course, winter ground school begins on 2026.12.02, ten evenings, Tuesday and Thursday, 19:00 to 21:00, at $680. That course is a separate booking, not part of the gift. The contact page has the address if you would rather write by post to Hangar 2.

Book a trial flight

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
SEVEN PRICES, USD

Fees

Every price on this page is in USD and is what Hibari Flight School charges at Brackmoor Airfield. The examiner's fee for a licence test is paid to the examiner.

Pay per lesson, or prepay ten hours

You can pay for dual flying as you go, at $245 per flight hour, or you can prepay a lesson block bundle of 10 flight hours for $2,350. The hours in that bundle are flown as ordinary lessons. Each time you are on the field the block is two hours: brief 25 min, walk-round 20 min, fly 60 min, debrief 15 min. Solo hire is a different line, at $195 per flight hour, and it applies once you are flying without an instructor. The office arranges either way of paying, Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00, on +1 555 0142 0911 or hello@hibariflight.example. If a morning is below minima and the school cancels by 07:00, you are not charged. A prepaid hour is not used. The flight is rebooked free. That rule is the same for a single lesson and for an hour drawn from the bundle.

What does a typical PPL cost?

Most students fly 50 to 60 hours before the test; budget from $13,500. That is an estimate, not a promise. The PPL minimum is 45 hours, and the span is usually 9 to 14 months if you keep coming through the weather at Brackmoor. The LAPL minimum is 30 hours, usually 6 to 10 months, and the LAPL budget starts from $9,200, also an estimate. Ground school at $680, the night rating at $1,350 if you add it after the PPL, and licence-test aircraft hire at $440 for up to 2 hours, are booked only if you need them. The examiner's fee sits outside all of these and is paid to the examiner. Flying more than the minimum is the ordinary pattern here. The school does not treat 50 to 60 hours as a target you must hit, and it does not treat $13,500 as a ceiling it can lock.

Dates already on the board

Two dates are already written up, and both use prices from the list above. On 2026.11.15 the trial-flight morning runs from 08:30 to 12:00. Each visitor's flight is $190 for 40 minutes airborne with a briefing, age 14 or over, up to 110 kg. On 2026.12.02 winter ground school begins: 10 evenings, Tuesday and Thursday, 19:00 to 21:00, at $680. Aisha Rahman leads that course. Neither date changes the dual rate of $245 or the solo rate of $195. The order the school teaches is trial flight, then ground school and dual, then first solo usually after 15 to 20 hours, then cross-country and the licence test. You can book the trial and leave the rest. Ines Laurent handles the booking at Hangar 2. The contact page carries the address, the phone and the hours.

Prices are the same in the hangar and on this page.

pages.title: Crew
pages.content:
SEVEN PEOPLE, HANGAR 2

Crew

Seven people run Hibari Flight School from Hangar 2. Two founded it in 2011, and the others joined between 2014 and 2021.

Margit Halvorsen

Head of training · since 2011

Margit Halvorsen is head of training and one of the two founders. She has been at Hibari Flight School since 2011, the year she and Ruth Abernathy opened Hangar 2 with two aircraft. The lesson students still fly is the shape she set: brief, walk-round, fly, debrief. A block is two hours on the field, split into 25, 20, 60 and 15 minutes. She teaches on the two-seat trainers from runway 09/27 at Brackmoor Airfield, and training questions from the other instructors come back to her. Trial flights, the PPL and the LAPL all sit under that same standard. The flying week she runs is Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset. The phrase she keeps on the school is the one on the door: read the wind, then fly.

Ruth Abernathy

Chief engineer · since 2011

Ruth Abernathy is chief engineer and the other founder. She has been at the school since 2011, when Hangar 2 opened with two aircraft. The fleet she looks after now is three two-seat low-wing trainers and one four-seat touring aircraft for cross-country. The machines students walk around, sample fuel from and fly are in her care. A twenty-minute walk-round means something because the propeller, the hinges and the fuel are her daily work, not a backdrop for a photograph. She is based at Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale, with the rest of the crew. If the question is really about a booking, it still belongs to the office rather than the hangar floor. Her name has been on the school since the first year, beside Margit Halvorsen's.

Tomás Ferreira

Flight instructor · since 2014

Tomás Ferreira is a flight instructor and has been at Hibari Flight School since 2014. He teaches on the two-seat trainers at Brackmoor, on the same circuit as every other instructor. A lesson with him is still 25 minutes of brief, 20 minutes of walk-round, 60 minutes in the air and 15 minutes of debrief. He joined after the school had already settled in Hangar 2, and by 2015 he was part of the flying week. Students on the PPL, the LAPL and the trial flight meet a named instructor on the apron and the same rules whoever the name is. Dual time is $245 per flight hour. The office assigns the day. The shape of the lesson does not change with the roster. Runway 09/27, grass 780 m and asphalt 640 m, is the runway he briefs.

Aisha Rahman

Instructor, ground-school lead · since 2016

Aisha Rahman is an instructor and the ground-school lead. She has been at Hibari Flight School since 2016. Ground school is the PPL theory course: 10 evenings at $680. Winter ground school begins on 2026.12.02 and meets on Tuesday and Thursday from 19:00 to 21:00. She also instructs in the air, on the same two-hour block as the rest of the crew, from runway 09/27. Theory and flying sit side by side on the licence path, which is why her work covers both the evening course and the aircraft. A visitor who only wants a trial flight, at $190, does not have to join the evenings. A student who continues toward the PPL, minimum 45 hours and usually 9 to 14 months, uses her course as well as the trainers. Book the evenings through the office.

Kwame Mensah

Instructor, night rating · since 2018

Kwame Mensah is an instructor for the night rating. He has been at Hibari Flight School since 2018. The night rating is 5 flight hours after the PPL and costs $1,350. He teaches it as its own course, with a brief and a debrief, not as an unplanned extra on an ordinary circuit. Daytime dual, the trial flight and the walk-round on the trainers are part of the instructor's week as well, and he shares that work with the crew. Published flying hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset. Bookings go through the office on +1 555 0142 0911. The five hours are the length of the course. They are not a promise about how many calendar weeks the rating will take when the weather is below minima and a morning is cancelled by 07:00.

Ines Laurent

Operations & bookings · since 2019

Ines Laurent runs operations and bookings. She has been at Hibari Flight School since 2019. She confirms a trial-flight morning, answers +1 555 0142 0911, and writes from hello@hibariflight.example. A confirmation e-mail goes out within one working day of you choosing a morning. The office is open Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00. When the weather is below minima she is part of the cancellation by 07:00, so the morning is not charged and can be rebooked free. Gift trial flights at $190, ordinary dual bookings at $245 an hour, and the prepaid bundle of 10 flight hours at $2,350 all pass her desk at Hangar 2. Ask for her if you want a named person on the booking. The address is Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale.

Jonah Petrakis

Instructor, tailwheel & cross-country · since 2021

Jonah Petrakis is an instructor for tailwheel and cross-country. He has been at Hibari Flight School since 2021, the latest arrival of the seven. Cross-country training uses the four-seat touring aircraft as well as the two-seat trainers. The school's story of Elena Duarte, from Brackmoor to Calder Field, 74 nm, is the kind of navigation flight this stage is for, once a student is past first solo. First solo itself usually comes after 15 to 20 hours. Jonah teaches inside the same lesson block as everyone else: brief, walk-round, fly, debrief. Tailwheel work is his other brief, on the school's aircraft, from runway 09/27. By 2024 he was already on the crew. That year marks a full roster, not a second founding. Book him through Ines Laurent's desk, in office hours.

pages.title: The Field
pages.content:
BRACKMOOR AIRFIELD

The Field

Brackmoor Airfield is a grass and asphalt field in Alder Vale. Hibari Flight School flies from Hangar 2, on runway 09/27.

Runway 09/27

Brackmoor Airfield's runway is 09/27. It has grass of 780 m and asphalt of 640 m, and Hibari Flight School uses both. A wide morning shows the hangar with its doors open, the windsock, trainers parked and a large soft sky. Students taxi the grass and fly the circuit that every lesson uses, the rounded pattern briefed before they walk out. The field is open Tuesday to Sunday, from 08:00 to sunset.

It is closed on Monday. Those are the flying hours. Office hours are shorter: Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00. Landing fees at Brackmoor are already inside the published prices, including the trial flight at $190 and the dual hour at $245. The school has flown this runway since Margit Halvorsen and Ruth Abernathy opened Hangar 2 in 2011.

The fleet

The fleet is three two-seat low-wing trainers and one four-seat touring aircraft for cross-country. The trainers are the aircraft used for trial flights, dual lessons and solo hire. The trial is $190 for 40 minutes airborne with a briefing. Dual is $245 per flight hour. Solo hire is $195 per flight hour. The touring aircraft carries the navigation lesson, the kind of flight in Elena Duarte's story from Brackmoor to Calder Field, 74 nm.

In 2011 the school opened with two aircraft in Hangar 2. The fleet named here is the one students walk around today. Ruth Abernathy, chief engineer since 2011, is responsible for all of them. A walk-round of 20 minutes, with a fuel sample held up to the light, is how each flying morning begins on whichever aircraft the lesson uses.

WEATHER MINIMA

Weather minima and the windsock

Grass 780 m and asphalt 640 m. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset.

A training flight goes ahead when the morning is within the school's minima. If it is below minima, the school cancels by 07:00, there is no charge, and the flight is rebooked free. The rule is the same for dual lessons, for an hour from the prepaid block of 10, and for a trial flight. The windsock on the boundary is there to be read. On a trial morning the instructor points it out, and on a lesson the student is expected to have looked before the brief.

The field board carries the next booked morning. It currently shows 2026.11.15 as a trial-flight morning from 08:30 to 12:00, and 2026.12.02 as the start of winter ground school. That ground school is 10 evenings, Tuesday and Thursday, 19:00 to 21:00. It is a classroom course, not a flying slot, and it costs $680.

Hangar 2 on Field Road

The school is Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale. That is the address for the office, the aircraft and the post. The phone is +1 555 0142 0911 and the e-mail is hello@hibariflight.example. Come by car along Field Road, or by bus on line 41, and look for the hangar. Directions are repeated on the contact page, and there is no map sitting in the page itself.

Cross-country lessons may land away, as on the route to Calder Field, 74 nm, but the brief starts here and the debrief of 15 minutes belongs back on this apron. Margit Halvorsen and Ruth Abernathy have worked from this hangar since 2011. The flying day is still Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset, and Monday the doors stay shut for flying.

See the field from the cockpit.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
HANGAR 2, FIELD ROAD

Contact

The office and the aircraft are both at Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield. Call, write, or come along Field Road.

Where to write, and where to call

The address is Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale. The phone is +1 555 0142 0911. The e-mail is hello@hibariflight.example. Ines Laurent handles operations and bookings, and she is the person to ask for when you call the office. A confirmation of a trial flight, or of any other booking, is sent by e-mail within one working day. Cross-country training may fly to Calder Field, 74 nm, but the desk that books it is this one.

For a gift trial flight, use the same phone and the same e-mail, and say that the $190 flight is a gift so the visitor's name is on the list for the morning. The school has been at this hangar since Margit Halvorsen and Ruth Abernathy opened it in 2011.

When is the office open, and when is the field open?

Office hours are Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00. Flying hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset. The field is closed on Monday. The office is closed on Sunday and on Monday. Sunday is still a flying day if you are already booked. Weather cancellations are made by 07:00, so a morning below minima is not charged and is rebooked free. The field board shows a trial-flight morning on 2026.11.15, from 08:30 to 12:00, and the start of winter ground school on 2026.12.02. Those ground-school evenings are Tuesday and Thursday, 19:00 to 21:00, ten evenings in the course, at $680. The evenings fall after the office has closed for the day. You book the course itself during office hours, with Aisha Rahman as the ground-school lead.

How do I get there by car or by bus?

By car, follow Field Road to Brackmoor Airfield and look for Hangar 2. The trainers are at the hangar, and the windsock stands on the boundary of runway 09/27, where the grass is 780 m and the asphalt is 640 m. By bus, take line 41 to the airfield and walk to Hangar 2 on Field Road. Line 41 is the bus that serves the field. This page does not include a map. The address is the direction: Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale. If you are coming for a trial flight, arrive 30 minutes early and bring photo identification. The limits are age 14 or over and up to 110 kg. For an ordinary lesson, come in time for the 25-minute brief so the block can run in order.

What should I ask for when I call?

Ask for a trial flight if you want 40 minutes airborne with a briefing at $190. Ask for dual lessons at $245 per flight hour, or for the prepaid bundle of 10 flight hours at $2,350. Ask for ground school if you want the PPL theory course at $680. Ask for the night rating, 5 flight hours at $1,350, only after the PPL. Kwame Mensah leads that course. If you are unsure between the PPL and the LAPL, say so on the call. The PPL minimum is 45 hours, usually 9 to 14 months, budget from $13,500. The LAPL minimum is 30 hours, usually 6 to 10 months, budget from $9,200. Both budgets are estimates, not promises. Solo hire, when you reach it, is $195 per flight hour. The medical, Class 2 or LAPL, is booked by you with an aviation medical examiner.

posts.title: A first trial flight on a still Saturday
posts.excerpt: Martin Okonjo visited Brackmoor for an introductory flight and took the controls above Alder Vale in clear, gentle morning air.
posts.content:
Martin Okonjo arrived at Hangar 2 thirty minutes early with his photo ID, as the confirmation said. The briefing took ten minutes, the walk-round another ten, and by half past eight he was strapped into the left seat.

Over the Vale the air was clear and still. He took the controls for most of the 40 minutes and landed on runway 09 with his instructor’s hands hovering, unused, near the stick.

posts.title: Priya’s first solo
posts.excerpt: Priya Nair flew her first solo at Hibari Flight School after 18 hours, on the circuit every lesson at Brackmoor follows.
posts.content:
Priya Nair flew her first solo from Brackmoor Airfield at 18 hours. At Hibari Flight School that step usually comes after 15 to 20 hours, so the morning was due in the only sense the school uses: the hours were in the usual band, and the instructor sent her.

She had learned the circuit the way everyone here learns it. Every lesson flies the same shape: brief, walk round, fly, debrief. A block on the field is two hours. Twenty-five minutes go to the plan, twenty minutes to the aircraft on the ground, sixty minutes to the flight, and fifteen minutes to the talk afterwards. Seventy minutes of the block are in the air or on the way to it. Runway 09/27 had become a place she could describe without the sketch. Grass 780 m, asphalt 640 m, the windsock on the boundary, Hangar 2 behind her with the doors open.

The brief on the solo morning was still 25 minutes. Her instructor sketched the rounded circuit and they both looked at the wind. The windsock is not there for the photograph. The school's line is to read the wind, then fly, and a first solo is a poor moment to skip the reading. They agreed the runway, the checks and the point at which she would come back and land. The clubhouse window faced the apron, as it does on any other brief. Nothing about the table was special. The decision sat in the hours she had already flown, not in a different script.

The walk-round took its 20 minutes. A fuel sample went up to the light. She put a hand along the wing and on the aileron hinge, and this time she was the one saying the sequence aloud, with the instructor listening. The aircraft was one of the three two-seat low-wing trainers kept at Hangar 2. Dual lessons up to that morning had been the published hour, $245, with aircraft, fuel, instructor and the landing fee at Brackmoor included. Solo hire, from this flight on, is the other published line, $195 per flight hour. The walk-round did not get shorter because the other seat was about to be empty.

Then the instructor stepped away. Priya was alone in the cockpit. She fastened the headset, looked once more toward the windsock, and flew the circuit they had just briefed. The picture kept from that morning is the one after landing: Priya in the cockpit with a thumbs-up, the instructor walking away across the foreground. What the picture leaves out is the debrief, because every block still ends with 15 minutes beside the parked aircraft. Headsets off. What matched the brief was said plainly, and so was what did not. The shape closed the way it had closed on every dual lesson since she started: brief, walk-round, fly, debrief.

Eighteen hours is not the licence. The PPL asks for a minimum of 45 hours, and most students at Hibari fly 50 to 60 hours before the test. The usual span is 9 to 14 months. Budget from $13,500, and that figure is an estimate, not a promise. Some students take the LAPL instead, at a minimum of 30 hours, usually 6 to 10 months, budget from $9,200. Priya's story records the solo hour. It does not record a finish date, and the school does not treat one student's morning as a timetable for the next.

The path after first solo is the same path written on the licence page. Ground school and dual already sit behind and beside the flying. Ground school is the PPL theory course of 10 evenings at $680, led by Aisha Rahman. Winter ground school begins on 2026.12.02, Tuesday and Thursday, 19:00 to 21:00. Cross-country comes later, on the four-seat touring aircraft as well as the trainers. Another story from the school follows Elena Duarte from Brackmoor to Calder Field, 74 nm. That is a later stage, not this one. The licence test, when a student reaches it, uses aircraft hire of up to 2 hours at $440. The examiner's fee is paid to the examiner.

Margit Halvorsen has been head of training since she and Ruth Abernathy opened the school in 2011. The solo standard Priya met is the one that training has used since then: same circuit, same two-hour block, same windsock. Tomás Ferreira, Aisha Rahman, Kwame Mensah and Jonah Petrakis teach inside that standard. Ines Laurent is the person who puts the next morning in the book, on +1 555 0142 0911 or at hello@hibariflight.example, from the office in Hangar 2, Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 17:00.

If the morning you want is not a solo at all, but a first look, the trial flight is the booking in Martin Okonjo's story as well as on the fees page. Forty minutes airborne, with a briefing, $190. Age 14 or over, up to 110 kg. Choose a morning online or by phone. A confirmation e-mail comes within one working day. On the day, arrive 30 minutes early with photo identification. The next trial-flight morning on the field board is 2026.11.15, from 08:30 to 12:00. If the weather is below minima, the school cancels by 07:00, there is no charge, and the flight is rebooked free. The field is open Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset, and closed on Monday. The address is Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale. Come by Field Road, or by bus on line 41, and read the windsock before you fly.

posts.title: Elena’s first cross-country
posts.excerpt: Elena Duarte navigated the cross-country route from Brackmoor to Calder Field and back, logging 74 nautical miles.
posts.content:
Elena Duarte navigated the cross-country route from Brackmoor to Calder Field and back, logging 74 nautical miles.

She planned it on the ground the evening before, checked the wind at the windsock in the morning and flew it with a map bag on her knee.

posts.title: Reading the windsock
posts.excerpt: A windsock tells you direction and strength at a glance. Here is what we look for before every sortie.
posts.content:
A windsock tells you the wind direction by where it points away from, and the strength by how far it stands out. Fully extended means roughly fifteen knots or more.

Before every sortie we walk out to it, look for a minute, and write down what we saw.

posts.title: Winter flying at Brackmoor
posts.excerpt: Short days, cold engines and clear air: what changes for students between November and February.
posts.content:
Winter days are short, so lesson blocks start earlier and the walk-round takes a little longer with frost on the wings.

The air is often the best of the year: dense, smooth and clear to the far end of the Vale.

posts.title: What ground school covers
posts.excerpt: Ten evenings, Tuesday and Thursday 19:00–21:00: the theory subjects behind the PPL examination.
posts.content:
The PPL theory course runs over ten evenings, Tuesday and Thursday 19:00–21:00, and costs $680.

It covers air law, navigation, meteorology, human performance, principles of flight and aircraft general knowledge.
